metadata.note: The Toledo, Peoria and Western - Effner (Indiana line) - Peoria - Keokuk, with the Hamilton - Warsaw and La Harpe - Lomax lines - drawn from the research report research/branches/toledo_peoria_and_western_railway.txt (companion site repo, 2026-10-08) and converted on 2026-10-08. Before this layer the map drew no TP&W route. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. The Peoria and Oquawka Eastern Extension, Logansport, Peoria and Burlington, Toledo, Peoria and Warsaw, TP&W Railroad (1880) and TP&W Railway (1887; restyled Railroad 1926-27) are successive names of one road and share one colour and one company string, as the Monon layer does for its names; the 1860-1875 features say 'TP&Warsaw era' in their labels. Nothing is drawn for the Wabash, St. Louis and Pacific lease (May 1880 - c.1884/85): no passenger timetable dated in those years has been found, so its Rule 4 Wabash-coloured split has no drawable year; the same holds for 1876-1886 generally. PRR (from 1893), CB&Q, McNear (1926-27), Santa Fe (1955) and PRR-Santa Fe joint (1960) stock control never changed who ran the trains and are not splits. The 1980-81 Amtrak Prairie Marksman over TP&W rails East Peoria - Chenoa is a separate Amtrak-coloured feature. Colour #C8008C is new to the dataset; its nearest existing colour is #B5179E (CIELAB dE 14.8).

properties.geometry_quality: 107.4 mi drawn Effner (Indiana state line) - Peoria Yard (East Peoria) against 108.0 mi in the 1952 Guide and Fowler. Traced end to end on OSM: 106.3 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=TP&W (today's Toledo, Peoria and Western Railway, operator TPW) and 1.4 mi on untagged rail in the same corridor. No straight-line leg. Every station waypoint (Sheldon, Watseka, Gilman, Chatsworth, Forrest, Fairbury, Chenoa, Meadows, Gridley, El Paso, Secor, Eureka, Washington, Farmdale) lies within 0.4 km of the line. The line ends at the TP&W yard in East Peoria (about 40.670, -89.542). LATER ALIGNMENT: this draws the present-day TP&W track for all years; line relocations since 1887, if any, are not researched.

segments.note: Toledo, Peoria and Western Railway (formed 28 Mar 1887 from the foreclosed TP&W Railroad) regular passenger trains, Effner (PRR connection) - Watseka - Gilman - Chatsworth - Fairbury - Chenoa - El Paso - Eureka - Washington - Peoria. The 1887 start is exact by company date; its trains are documented that summer (the Peoria - Niagara Falls excursion wrecked at Chatsworth on 10 Aug 1887, 80+ killed). In this era trains ran through to Peoria Union Depot across the TP&W's own Illinois River bridge, but only 1887 is confirmed for that crossing (see tpw-illinois-river-crossing), so this feature stops at Peoria Yard. Ridership fell from 1,067,416 (1911) to 260,747 (1925); by 1926 only one train each way. The 1926/1927 boundary with the mixed-train era is secondary-sourced and conflicts (Trains: mixed before the 1926 foreclosure; tpwrailroad site: 1927) - treat it as approximate. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1887 start from the company date and the 10 Aug 1887 Chatsworth wreck; decline figures and the 1926/1927 end of regular trains from american-rails.com, Trains Magazine and the tpwrailroad site, which conflict; all as gathered by research/branches/toledo_peoria_and_western_railway.txt (companion site repo, 2026-10-08). Traced 1.0 mi on OSM: 0.7 mi on TP&W-tagged track west from the yard to where it ends at 40.6670, -89.5611, and the rest on untagged rail. APPROXIMATED: one straight-line leg of 2.1 mi from 40.6670, -89.5611 (East Peoria) to the Peoria Union Depot site at 40.6845, -89.5942 (Wikipedia coordinates for the 1882 station on Depot Street between State and Oak Streets, demolished). The TP&W's own Illinois River bridge (the 1857 Peoria and Oquawka crossing; destroyed by a barge tow 12 Feb 1970) is NOT in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap and its exact site was not located, so the straight line stands in for it - it does not show where the bridge was. The present-day route over the Peoria and Pekin Union bridge (a 1970-onward FREIGHT detour) is deliberately NOT drawn.

segments.note: ANCHOR: the single confirmed year in which a TP&W Railway passenger train crossed the Illinois River between East Peoria and Peoria Union Depot - the 10 Aug 1887 Peoria - Niagara Falls excursion departed Peoria eastbound through Eureka and Chenoa. Through trains Effner - Peoria - Keokuk almost certainly crossed here every year until some date before Sept 1942, when the Guide shows east trains ending at Peoria Yard and west trains starting at Peoria; when the cut-back happened is not established (plausibly with the 1928 East Peoria yard or the 1926-27 cut to mixed trains - a guess). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed; do not widen this anchor without a dated timetable. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 112.5 mi drawn Peoria Union Depot - Keokuk Union Depot against 112.8 mi documented (Peoria MP 111.1 - Keokuk MP 223.9, 1952 Guide and Fowler agree). No straight-line leg, apart from a 0.2 mi connector from the Union Depot site (40.6845, -89.5942) to the first traced vertex. FOREIGN TRACK: Peoria - Hollis (7.5 mi drawn, 7.5 mi documented) is TP&W trackage rights and is drawn on present-day untagged terminal track - southwest along the Peoria riverfront beside the BNSF Peoria Subdivision to about 40.659, -89.636, then south past the Iowa Junction area to Hollis (40.597, -89.670). Historically the TP&W ran over the Peoria and Pekin Union Peoria - Iowa Jct - Hollis until c.1928, then over the CB&Q to Iowa Junction and the Peoria Railway Terminal to Hollis (Fowler IL 224 note); OSM does not tag which present-day track was whose, so this drawing does not distinguish the two routes and may follow neither exactly. Hollis - Keokuk (105.0 mi drawn vs 105.3) is on ways tagged old_railway_operator=TP&W (Keokuk Junction Railway today, part of it disused west of La Harpe), plus about 1.6 mi of untagged rail at the Keokuk end. Elvaston - Hamilton - Keokuk includes ways tagged 'joint (TP&W/Wabash)' - the Wabash Keokuk branch drawn in wabash_railroad.geojson shares this end. The Mississippi crossing is the present Keokuk Municipal (Keokuk and Hamilton) bridge, a 1916 replacement on the 1871 site - a LATER STRUCTURE than the 1887-1915 years. Ends at Keokuk Union Depot (40.3906, -91.3817, Wikipedia; opened 1891, TP&W a founding tenant); 1887-1890 trains used an earlier Keokuk station not located. Every waypoint (Hollis, Mapleton, Glasford, Canton, Cuba, Smithfield, Marietta, Bushnell, Blandinsville, La Harpe, Ferris, Elvaston) within 0.8 km of the line; Hamilton station 1.0 km.

segments.note: Toledo, Peoria and Western Railway regular passenger trains, Peoria (Union Depot) - Hollis - Mapleton - Glasford - Canton - Cuba - Bushnell - Blandinsville - La Harpe - Ferris - Elvaston - Hamilton - Keokuk, over P&PU (later CB&Q / Peoria Railway Terminal) trackage rights Peoria - Hollis and the Keokuk and Hamilton bridge into Iowa. 1887 start exact by company date. Fowler marks Leaman in the 1893 Guide, confirming the main line that year. Regular trains ended c.1926-27 (sources conflict, see tpw-effner-peoria-yard). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Peoria and Oquawka (Eastern Extension) 1860-61, Logansport, Peoria and Burlington 1861-64, Toledo, Peoria and Warsaw from 14 May 1864 (receivership 20 Jan 1875) - successive names of the road that became the Toledo, Peoria and Western, drawn in its one colour. The Keokuk and Hamilton bridge (2,190 ft, 378 ft draw) opened 15 Jun 1871 after work begun Apr 1869, giving the Toledo, Peoria and Warsaw its Keokuk terminus. Fowler shows 1868-70 Guide letters at East Keokuk and 1875 Official Guide letters on the line; 1875 is the last confirmed year. This end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 9.2 mi drawn La Harpe - Disco - Lomax against 10.5 mi documented (La Harpe MP 195.5 - Lomax MP 206.0, 1952 Guide). Traced on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=TP&W (Keokuk Junction Railway today); no straight-line leg. The drawing ends where the TP&W meets the BNSF (ex-CB&Q) line at 40.6803, -91.0565, about 0.9 mi east of Lomax station (waypoint 1.4 km off), and starts at the junction 150 m from the main line west of La Harpe - which accounts for most of the 1.3 mi shortfall. NOT DRAWN: the 1875 trains continued 9 mi from Lomax to Burlington, Iowa over CB&Q trackage rights; that leg is CB&Q geometry and is left off.

segments.note: ANCHOR. Peoria and Oquawka (Eastern Extension) 1860-61, Logansport, Peoria and Burlington 1861-64, Toledo, Peoria and Warsaw from 14 May 1864 (receivership 20 Jan 1875) - successive names of the road that became the Toledo, Peoria and Western, drawn in its one colour. La Harpe - Disco - Lomax was completed 26 Nov 1871 to give a second CB&Q interchange and an entry to Burlington. The only confirmed passenger year is 1875: Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letter at Disco, Iowa and Burlington. Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed; passenger use at opening is not established. By the table dated Sept 1942 (printed Feb 1952) the line was 'Freight Service only' and Disco carries the freight-only dagger in the index, so NO TP&W Railway-era (1887+) year is drawn - Rule 1. McNear dropped the Burlington trackage rights c.1927-28 (american-rails.com), a plausible but unproven passenger end. Do not widen this anchor without a dated timetable. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler IL 225 1875 Official Guide letters at Disco, Iowa and Burlington; 26 Nov 1871 completion (american-rails.com); 1952 Guide 'Freight Service only' for the 1887+ era (as read by the research report research/branches/toledo_peoria_and_western_railway.txt (companion site repo, 2026-10-08); not re-read in the tracing pass). Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: Amtrak's state-supported Prairie Marksman, Chicago - East Peoria, ran over the TP&W East Peoria - Farmdale - Washington - Eureka - El Paso - Gridley - Meadows - Chenoa from 10 Aug 1980 to 4 Oct 1981: one round trip, a morning departure from a small metal depot in the East Peoria yard and an evening return. It followed the Rock Island's end of Peoria - Chicago service at the start of 1979. Amtrak ran the train, so it carries Amtrak's colour (Rule 4), on TP&W rails. Headway from the one daily round trip (Trains).
